## Web Searcher: Batched QR tensor core GPU

Research question: "Research state-of-the-art and NOVEL techniques for a FAST BATCHED SQUARE Householder QR factorization on an NVIDIA B200 (sm_100, Blackwell, TF32/tf32x3 tensor cores, CUDA 12.8, Triton 3.6 + Gluon/TLX, PyTorch 2.11), written as CUSTOM kernels (Triton first, CUDA/CuTe DSL for more control — NOT library calls). I have an existing blocked compact-WY implementation at 2388us geomean (rank #5); competitors WITHOUT NVFP4 reach ~1360us (1.3-1.8x faster), so reachable headroom provably exists. I need techniques to BEAT it, and I may need to invent new ones — propose novel combinations, not just a catalog.

EXACT OUTPUT CONTRACT (this is the binding constraint): output must be packed (H, tau) such that a checker computes Q = torch.linalg.householder_product(tril(H,-1), tau), R = triu(H), and requires (in FP64): ||R - Q^T A|| <= 20*n*eps32 * ||A||, ||Q^T Q - I|| <= 100*n*eps32, and tril(Q^T A, -1) ~ 0. So ANY valid FLAT global Householder representation (H, tau) passes — it need NOT match LAPACK bit-for-bit, but Q must be A's true orthogonal factor and the reflectors must compose as ONE global householder_product sequence (per-panel/per-block reflectors that don't compose globally FAIL). Inputs include ill-conditioned, rank-deficient, near-rank-deficient, clustered-singular-value, near-collinear, banded, and row-scaled matrices, so the method must be numerically robust (naive CholeskyQR that squares the condition number FAILS the ill-conditioned cases).

THE BOTTLENECK: after optimizing the trailing-update GEMMs (already at tensor-core roofline / minimal-MMA round-to-nearest precision), the PANEL FACTORIZATION (the tall-skinny n x IB QR with its SERIAL reflector-by-reflector dependency chain) is now ~45% of runtime and is the critical path. The dominant shapes are batch=640/n=512, batch=60/n=1024 (grid-starved: 60 thread-blocks on 148 SMs leaves most idle during the panel), batch=8/n=2048, batch=2/n=4096.

I need, with code-level specificity and URL citations:
1. HOUSEHOLDER RECONSTRUCTION from communication-avoiding QR: the LAPACK xORHR_COL / xUNHR_COL routine and the Ballard-Demmel-Grigori-Hoemmen-Knight (2014/2015) "Reconstructing Householder vectors from TSQR" method. How to make the reconstruction step CHEAP (it is currently O(batch * n^3) and eats the panel savings) — can the reconstruction itself be tensor-core GEMM-heavy and parallel? Exact recurrences.
2. TSQR / CAQR (communication-avoiding QR): the row-block-tree panel factorization that replaces the serial reflector chain with O(log P) tree-reduction, filling idle SMs at grid-starved batch. How to combine TSQR (which gives R + an implicit Q) with ORHR_COL to emit FLAT geqrf-compatible (H, tau). Per-leaf and merge recurrences; how to map the tree to one-CTA-per-row-block on a GPU without O(n) device-wide barriers.
3. PANEL CRITICAL-PATH SHORTENING that is NOT communication-avoiding: the UT-transform / compact-WY-T-only formulation, recursive/divide-and-conquer panel (geqrt3), look-ahead, and any 2023-2026 GPU technique that shortens the serial Householder dependency chain length (not just GEMM-ifies the trailing apply).
4. BATCHED QR specifically: MAGMA batched geqrf, cuSOLVER batched, and any recent (2023-2026) papers on batched small/medium QR on tensor-core GPUs — what algorithm do they use for the panel, and how do they handle the batch=640/n=512 (GPU-saturating) vs batch=2/n=4096 (GPU-starved) regimes differently?
5. MIXED-PRECISION robust QR: tf32x3/error-corrected-TF32 and 3xTF32 emulation for the panel reflector formation (not just the trailing), and iterative refinement / re-orthogonalization schemes that keep flat-(H,tau) FP32 accuracy on ill-conditioned/rank-deficient inputs.
6. A RANKED list of 3-5 DISTINCT, concrete, buildable approaches (each with the key numerical risk and the cheapest decisive experiment to validate it) to shorten the panel critical path while still emitting exact flat (H, tau) — prioritized for the batch=640/n=512 and batch=60/n=1024 regimes that dominate the geomean. Explicitly include any NOVEL combination you can construct from the above primitives, even if not published."

Your angle: **Batched QR tensor core GPU** — 
Search query: `batched QR factorization MAGMA cuSOLVER geqrfBatched tensor core Blackwell H100 2024 2025 panel algorithm`

## Main Publication

Since 2017, NVIDIA GPUs have been equipped with specialized units known as Tensor Cores, which have been explored for matrix factorization, such as QR factorization. The most directly relevant 2024-2025 work is:

**"High Performance Householder QR Factorization on Emerging GPU Architectures Using Tensor Cores"** published in IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems, Volume 36, Issue 3, pages 422-436 (March 2025) by Leng, Zou, Wang, Wu, and Zhang.

## Key Technical Approaches

The paper addresses a fundamental challenge: the inside GEMMs (General Matrix Multiplications) in QR factorization are typically tall and skinny, and compared to compute-bound square GEMMs, these tall and skinny GEMMs are memory bound, leading to suboptimal performance on Tensor Cores.

The solution involves: recursive QR factorization can convert the tall and skinny GEMMs to relatively square and large GEMMs, resulting in better performance on Tensor Cores.

## Mixed Precision Support

The work extends FP16 Tensor-Cores-based QR factorization to accommodate FP32 and FP64 on FP16 and INT8 Tensor Cores, respectively. Additionally, to address the issue of orthogonality loss, the authors transition from the Gram-Schmidt to the Householder algorithm while preserving high performance.

results.title: High Performance Householder QR Factorization on Emerging GPU Architectures Using Tensor Cores (Leng, Zou, Wang, Wu, Zhang — IEEE TPDS 36(3):422-436, Mar 2025)
results.snippet: The single most on-target paper. Directly attacks the original question's exact bottleneck: the inner QR GEMMs are tall-and-skinny and memory-bound on tensor cores. Its core technique is RECURSIVE QR factorization (geqrt3-style divide-and-conquer panel) to convert tall-skinny GEMMs into square/large GEMMs that hit tensor-core roofline — this is precisely the 'panel critical-path shortening that is NOT communication-avoiding' the user asked for (item 3). Covers mixed precision: extends FP16-tensor-core QR to FP32 (via FP16 tensor cores, i.e. error-corrected / split emulation analogous to 3xTF32) and FP64 (via INT8 cores), and explicitly switches Gram-Schmidt -> Householder to fix orthogonality loss on ill-conditioned inputs (item 5). Maps to the trailing-update GEMM-ification plus the recursive panel. ACM mirror DOI 10.1109/TPDS.2024.3522776 is paywalled; IEEE Xplore is the canonical landing page.

results.title: Batch QR Factorization on GPUs: Design, Optimization, and Tuning (Boukaram/Abdelfattah et al., ICCS 2022 — MAGMA batched geqrf)
results.snippet: The canonical MAGMA batched-geqrf design paper and the direct answer to item 4 (batched QR, GPU-saturating vs GPU-starved regimes). Documents the THREE-strategy switch by matrix size: (a) fully-fused single-kernel factorization for n<=32, (b) fused panel+update kernels for medium sizes, (c) classical LAPACK-style blocked panel + batch-GEMM trailing for large sizes — exactly the regime-dependent dispatch the user needs for batch=640/n=512 (saturating) vs batch=2/n=4096 (starved). Reports MAGMA up to 2.3x/3.3x (s/d) over KBLAS and 16-25x over cuBLAS via aggressive batch-GEMM use. Sections explicitly cover panel optimization (5.5), trailing update (6), and sub-warp tuning (7). Mirror also at iccs-meeting.org/archive/iccs2022/papers/133500064.pdf.

results.title: Implementation of QR factorization of tall and very skinny matrices on current GPUs (Jonas Thies & Melven Röhrig-Zöllner, 2026)
results.snippet: Newest result (2026, H100-targeted) and squarely on the panel/TSQR critical path that is now ~45% of the user's runtime. Tall-and-VERY-skinny is exactly the n x IB panel shape and the grid-starved regime (batch=60/n=1024). Includes H100 roofline models and benchmarks vs library baselines (filenames confirm cuSOLVER/MAGMA-style comparisons). Most directly informs how to keep the tall-skinny panel reduction bandwidth-bound-optimal and fill idle SMs — the core of items 2 and 6. Worth fetching the full text from arxiv.org/abs/2603.20889 for the per-leaf/merge recurrences.

results.title: Communication-Avoiding QR Decomposition for GPUs (Anderson, Ballard, Demmel, Keutzer — LAWN 240 / UCB-EECS)
results.snippet: The canonical CAQR/TSQR-on-GPU reference, directly answering item 2 (row-block reduction tree replacing the serial reflector chain with O(log P) tree-reduction to fill idle SMs at grid-starved batch). Demmel is also a co-author of the Ballard-Demmel-Grigori-Hoemmen-Knight 'reconstructing Householder vectors from TSQR' work the user cites in item 1, so this is the upstream primitive for combining TSQR (implicit Q) with ORHR_COL to emit flat geqrf-compatible (H,tau). Describes mapping one-CTA-per-row-block and avoiding device-wide barriers. Reports speedups over MAGMA. Foundational for any TSQR-based panel design.

results.title: Batched QR and SVD Algorithms on GPUs with Applications in Hierarchical Matrix Compression (Boukaram, Turkiyyah, Keyes — Parallel Computing 2018 / KBLAS)
results.snippet: The KBLAS-batched-QR paper and the chief competitor MAGMA benchmarks against. Relevant to item 4: targets exactly the batch-of-small/medium-matrices regime (the batch=640/n=512 case) and the data-reuse-via-shared-memory strategy that caches the whole panel in fast memory for few-row matrices — the alternative to GEMM-ification when the matrix is small enough to fit on-chip. Useful as the design contrast to MAGMA's batch-GEMM approach for choosing the per-regime panel kernel.

results.title: High Accuracy Low Precision QR Factorization and Least Square Solver on GPU with TensorCore (Zhang, Baboulin et al., 2019)
results.snippet: Directly relevant to item 5 (mixed-precision robust QR on tensor cores). Establishes the FP16/TF32-tensor-core QR baseline plus iterative-refinement / re-orthogonalization to recover FP32-level accuracy and orthogonality on ill-conditioned inputs — the accuracy-recovery scheme needed to keep flat-(H,tau) valid against the checker's 20*n*eps32 / 100*n*eps32 bounds when forming reflectors in reduced precision. The precursor that the 2025 TPDS tensor-core paper builds on; ar5iv HTML version is readable at ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1912.05508.
